text:
Nina: Strange mypy/pyright behavior with autogenerated models + async sample app. It rejects `None` for an Optional[List[str]] field when passed as kwarg. runtime works. tiny repro below.

Nina: repro:
```py
# generated model (runtime)
class FeatureFlags(BaseModel):
    flags: Optional[list[str]] = None

async def make():
    f = FeatureFlags(flags=None)  # pyright: "Argument of type 'None' is not assignable to parameter of type 'list[str]'"
    return await AsyncClient.create(flags=f)
```

Nina: note: the generated wheel we install contains .pyi stubs where the field is `flags: list[str]` (missing Optional). So typechecker thinks kwarg can't be None.

Omar: ah, so this is a stub drift bug: codegen generates Optional in runtime model, but packaging step strips Optional in the pyi. Likely a serialization step in our typegen that collapses union with list generics.

Priya: I've hit similar when mypy/pyright parse `list[str] | None` vs `Optional[list[str]]` differently if the pyi generator normalizes typing to `list[str]` by mistake. Does this happen only for union with generics?

Nina: seems specific to generic containers. I ran `python -m pip unpack` on the wheel and inspected `redwood_sdk/models.pyi` 16 it has `flags: list[str]` (no Optional). The runtime `models.py` has `flags: Optional[list[str]] = None`.

Omar: short-term workaround for sample apps: explicitly construct with `FeatureFlags(flags=cast(Optional[list[str]], None))` or use positional `FeatureFlags(None)`. Not great for users.

Priya: action items: 1) fix typegen to preserve Optional on generic container unions; 2) add unit test in packaging that compares runtime annotations with generated stubs; 3) add a changelog note. I can take 1 and 2.

Build Bot: CI: sampleapps/typing-check failed in mypy/pyright step. Linked issue https://github.com/redwood/inference/issues/5490 (label: dx:typing).

Omar: tiny PR idea: when generating pyi, run `get_type_hints()` on the runtime model and serialize exact string form (i.e., keep Optional[]) rather than re-rendering AST nodes which lose Optionals on generics. That should be a low-risk patch.

Nina: thanks. adding a minimal sampleapp commit to the issue so QA can reproduce on different py versions. Also requested backport to 0.13.x since a few customers hit this in strict-pyright CI.

Priya: will open PR and add test that fails on current generator. ETA: 1 day. Assign to @Omar for review.

Nina: appreciate it 90. Will follow up once PR lands.
